newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse seen consolidating then rising.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse seen consolidating then rising.

text.p: The Brussels bourse, which on Friday paused for breath despite a solid overnight performance in New York, is expected to consolidate in coming days before rising once more, traders said.
"Sometimes it is necessary for a market to take a breath after a long rise. But the fundamentals are all good so we are not worried it might go down," one trader said.
Traders said there was no other explanation for the relatively poor performance of the Belgian market against its European neighbours.
"It was a Friday mood. It was very quiet," one said.
Traders said the strong dollar and low long-term interest rates coupled with positive underlying sentiment all augured well for the bourse.
There were few outstanding performances on the Brussels market on Friday.
Retailer Delhaize was one of the more memorable stocks, slipping 50 francs to 1,995 with nearly 150,000 shares changing hands.
Traders said most of the selling had come from U.K. and U.S. investors after brokerage Morgan Stanley removed the stock from one of its Belgian portfolios.
Chemicals firm Solvay, under pressure since reporting disappointing 1996 results, had a good day rising 300 francs to close at 21,100 france as buyers returned.
"Buyers came in when the stock went below 21,000 but the volume was quite thin. The stock is still a hold," one trader said.
Reuters Securities 3000 also shows the Solvay stock is approaching oversold levels.
Another notable performer was metals group Union Miniere which rose 60 francs to 2,630 as buyers continued to buy the stock on the basis of the dollar and zinc prices.
However, Reuters Securities 3000 indicates the stock is in overbought territory -- and traders agreed.

"It is in the middle of a major restructuring, but the benefits will not show through until 1999 so we think it is a bit early to be pushing the stock now," one trader said. "We rate is as overbought."
The Bel-20 share index ended 0.89 points down at 2,098.03 with eight gainers and 12 losers. Just under three billion francs of Belgian shares changed hands.
